title: Jesse Minter Announces Joe Fagnano As Starting Quarterback vs. Jaguars
headline: Joe Fagnano starts at QB Thursday vs. Jacksonville; Lamar Jackson's availability is still undetermined and Tyler Huntley is out, possibly heading to IR.
summary: Minter confirmed that Joe Fagnano will start at quarterback Thursday night against Jacksonville, calling it an opportunity and saying the team is excited to play in front of its fans. He praised Fagnano for taking advantage of his chances since training camp, noting that he got few reps in OTAs because of the quarterback numbers but gained more work after an injury at the position about ten days before the first preseason game. Minter described Fagnano as calm and composed, said the offense ran smoothly with him in the preseason, and said the familiarity with terminology and calls from past stints should help him operate on a short week. He said the other leaders have responded well and laid out the formula for winning: run the ball, protect and play well around Fagnano, and make game-changing plays on defense and special teams. On Jacksonville, Minter pointed to their physical run and pass game, strong backs who break tackles, skill players like Parker Washington, and Trevor Lawrence and Liam Coen's offense. He said the team would need to stop the run and make plays on defense. Asked about Lamar Jackson's status for this week, Minter said the team would know the final answer at some point before Thursday. He said Tyler Huntley is out and could be placed on IR, with more details expected soon.

title: Jesse Minter Discusses Quarterback Injuries
headline: Joe Fagnano is expected to get a chance to start Thursday vs. Jacksonville, while Lamar Jackson's timetable is undetermined and Tyler Huntley is unlikely to play this week.
summary: Minter said the team is about 70 hours from a Thursday night home game against a good Jacksonville team and that players came in ready to work. He expects Joe Fagnano to have a chance to play Thursday, though he is dealing with a couple of issues and the starter decision is still being worked through over the next day or two. Minter said the team will get extra reps in walkthroughs for players who have seen less playing time. On Lamar Jackson, he said a more definitive timetable might come sometime this week, that surgery has not yet happened, and he would not specify the injury type. Tyler Huntley is still working through an injury and is probably not available this week, with the longer-term picture to be determined. Minter said he expects Roger Rosengarten's comments about feeling responsible for Lamar's injury were a product of his competitiveness, and he rejected the idea that the team blames him. On defense, Minter said the unit competed but gave up explosive plays that swung the game, and that the team's offensive line needs improvement in pass protection and the run game.

title: Dave Canales: 'There’s an urgency about the group right now'
headline: Bryce Young looked great in his first practice back and the offense's book is fully open; Damien Lewis (knee) was limited and day-to-day, with guards Simpkins and Bullock also back on the field.
summary: Canales opened by saying Brady Christensen returned to practice and it was good to see him battling with teammates again. He said Bryce Young looked great, moved around well, and was ready after a varied practice, and that Young's mobility concerns have not changed the play calls, with the whole playbook open. He credited the team's response after an emotional stretch, citing an urgency and a need to rally around solutions and stack consistency. On defense, he said AC now coaches the whole front, including the outside linebackers and defensive tackles, so interim coordinator Todd Wash can focus on the coordinator role, and Pete still coaches linebackers. He said the team is built to play a 3-4 but would not detail base-defense plans for the week. On injuries, Damien Lewis was limited and could not finish practice, with his status day to day pending how his knee responds, while guards Torricelli Simpkins and Corey Bullock took part, with the next-day reaction to decide their status. Asked about trades and the deadline, he deferred to the GM and quarterbacks coach and said the roster depth and comfort level with trading contributors factor in. His top defensive priority for Sunday against Denver is stopping the run, and he praised Denver's disciplined, close-game-winning approach under Sean Payton and Vance Joseph.

title: Ben Johnson: 'These guys earned this victory ... I couldn't be more proud of them' | Press Conference
headline: Swift's workload (27 carries, 3 TDs) and Caleb Williams' trust-building praise stand out; Grady Jarrett (groin) and Kentavius Street (knee) are unclear for a short week.
summary: Ben Johnson credited the team's physical, composed play in the 34-17 win over Seattle and said the team responded well after several momentum swings. He praised the Seahawks as a strong team with a top-tier defense and special teams unit. He said the opening drive was a product of patience and the running game forcing favorable down-and-distance. Johnson highlighted Rhamondre-style grinding from D'Andre Swift, saying every yard he gained was earned on 27 attempts with three touchdowns. He said Caleb Williams took care of the football, played well in coverage, and has advanced far enough in the offense that he can absorb a more elaborate game plan quickly. Johnson was bothered by pre-snap penalties, including two delay-of-game and false-start calls, though he said the crowd did not excuse them. He said Grady Jarrett (groin) and Kentavius Street (knee) were injured, with the status to be determined as the team prepares for a short week before the bye.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Justin Herbert's Performance and Continued Team Improvement
headline: Harbaugh says David Njoku's practice window is opening soon, Rodney Shelley and Donte Jackson are ramping up, and Khalil Mack is staying put, while the backfield rotation is under review after a poor running game.
summary: Harbaugh gave a practice update that is partly garbled in the captions. Rodney Shelley and Donte Jackson are ramping up in practice, and another player is expected to start working in soon. Brenen Thompson is not likely to practice this week, and Deane Leonard remains in the concussion protocol. Harbaugh expects the Leonard situation to open David Njoku's practice window. He praised the offensive linemen who moved positions and called Joe Alt an elite player. On the trade deadline, Harbaugh said his focus is on the Texans, but the organization is always looking to improve. He said he wants Khalil Mack to stay, calling him a pillar of the team who wants to be here. On Justin Herbert, he said Herbert mostly does his job well and that only two throws he would like back. He acknowledged the offense has not finished drives, with the touchdown drought and the lack of third-down success as the key issues. He said the running game was not its best and that the team is looking at rotating its three healthy backs more effectively, possibly giving one a longer run. On the defense, he praised Tarheeb Still as a favorite player and Isas Waxter for rising, and said the unit has responded well despite playing without Derwin James.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Nov 2 | Press Conference
headline: Kingston impressed in his first start at guard and could start again; Jaylen Wright is trusted in kick returns, while Kadyn Proctor remains in protocol.
summary: Hafley said Kadyn Proctor is still in protocol and progressing through the steps, with no firm timetable. He was positive on Malik Willis, citing clean decisions, a touchdown pass and third-down conversions, while calling out areas to improve in throwing, running and decision-making. He praised Jarrett Kingston's first start at guard, saying he started slow but got physical and finished well, and said he will be ready if needed again. He said the defense played better situationally against New England, with better third downs and second-and-long, though missed opportunities on big plays hurt. He defended Chris, who had a deep-pass breakdown, and said he would move on from it. On Ollie Gordon, he said emotional penalties, both pre- and post-snap, are unacceptable and that he is addressing them directly. He praised the rookie receivers and Malik Washington's touchdown drive, and said Kaytron Allen is earning trust on special teams with his backfield role possibly coming soon. Jaylen Wright was a bright spot in the return game, and Hafley said his confidence in Wright as a runner has not changed. He said the kicker, Zayne Anderson, will stay in the job for now after the missed kick.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Discusses The Week 8 Loss To The Bears
headline: Leonard Williams (stinger) is questionable, the running backs left the game 'okay,' and Macdonald expects Darnold's quicker-release emphasis to continue on a short week.
summary: Macdonald credited the Bears for winning in all three phases and said Seattle lost in all three as well, with the margins too small when the fundamentals slip. He framed the short turnaround as the first of several this season and said the focus is on getting players' bodies and minds ready for Wednesday, with no time for lingering on the loss. On the run game, he said he didn't have a great answer yet, citing offensive line changes, and that the team will stay together and find solutions. He declined to discuss running back play counts but said the game's flow affected how players were used. On Sam Darnold, he wants to keep encouraging him to use his legs and athleticism, while the coaches design and coach early-down efficiency so throws come on time. He also said kickoff return timing needs to improve and that better execution should spread the ball more evenly across the offense. On injuries, he said the running backs came out of the game okay, Leonard Williams has a stinger and his status will be determined later, and he mentioned a foot injury to Connor O'Toole. He had no update on Quenton Nelson's performance.
